newsitem.title: GERMANY: Home Shopping Network invests in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Home Shopping Network invests in Germany.

text.p: Home Shopping Network (HSN), the U.S. television retail group, has taken a stake of 29 percent in Home Order Television (H.O.T.), Germany's first TV shopping channel, H.O.T. said on Tuesday.
Existing shareholders will lower their stakes in H.O.T. to make room for HSN. No financial details were disclosed.

Quelle Schickedanz AG & Co will cut its stake to 31 percent from 50 percent. Thomas Kirch, son of Bavarian media magnate Leo Kirch, will cut his share to 33 percent from 40 percent previously. Georg Kofler, head of broadcaster Pro Sieben Media AG, will trim his stake to seven percent from ten percent.
Home Shopping Network invests in Germany
The German home shopping channel was launched in October last year initially as a pilot project in Bavaria.

The H.O.T. network expects to achieve 65 million marks ($42.3 million) in sales this year. It said earlier this year it expected to break even by the year 2000 when sales are expected to rise to 300 million marks a year.
Shortly after its 1995 debut, H.O.T. faced a regulatory challenge from rival broadcaster RTL, which is majority owned by Bertelsmann and Cie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion .

RTL, citing a legal ban on home-shopping programming during certain hours, said it felt it was placed at a competitive disadvantage and appealed to Bavarian media regulators to block H.O.T. from being broadcast nationally via the Astra satellite.
The challenge was rejected in a court ruling.

H.O.T. has been broadcasting nationally via the Astra direct-to-home satellite system since December 1995. Via satellite alone, it reaches more than five million households, or more than half of all households with satellite hook-ups.

The shopping channel is also broadcast to cable TV subsribers in Munich, Nuremberg and Saxony- Anhalt and an additional seven million households in Frankfurt, Dresden and Leipzig receive one-hour chunks of H.O.T. via local cable stations.
The network said last week that it aimed to boost the number of households that receive its programming to 10 million in three years.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.537 German Marks)
